title: fix(app-shell): Studio shows the flow state the deployment runs, alike in the rail, the header and Problems (objectui#11779)
body:
Fixes #11779

Clause-②: no

Implemented by the os-dev agent dispatched by the seat 3 `domain:ui` PM under claim comment 6046146169, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8`.

## What an author reads now

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Header **Trigger** of a record-triggered flow | `autolaunched` (the flow-level `type`) | `Record updated · task` (the Start node's event and object) |
| Header **Status** of a published flow with no `status` key | `draft` (grey) | `On`, from the engine's runtime row, as in the rail |
| A schedule flow the deployment does not arm (scheduled work switched off) | rail: green `On`, the reason only on hover; header: `active`; Problems: "No problems" | rail and header: grey `Not running here`, the platform's reason as hover text; Problems: a note carrying the reason, not counted |
| A flow that declares no trigger | rail `On` | unchanged: `On`, titled "no trigger (run manually)" |
| A new flow's switch, under "Off by default · review before enabling" | `Enabled` | `Disabled` (saved with `status: 'obsolete'`) |

## How

- **One derivation.** `deriveFlowRunStatus` (in `flow-problems.ts`) maps the engine's runtime row to one of `on` / `manual` / `not-running` / `off`; with no row it reads `unpublished` (the host read `_status` and the engine has no row for the flow) or, with no runtime reading at all, the draft's own switch (`enabled` / `disabled`, read the way the engine reads `status`: `obsolete` and `invalid` off, anything else on). `describeFlowRunStatus` is the one wording of those states. The rail's `FlowStatusDot`, the header's Status pill and the Problems panel's note all read these two functions.
- **The hand-off.** The Automations pillar gives the open flow's `_status` row to the preview through `FlowRuntimeContext` (a row, `null` for no row, nothing while no runtime answer is in). It is a context rather than a `MetadataPreviewProps` member, so the published preview contract does not change. A host with no provider (the metadata-admin page) gets the draft-switch reading, so a flow with no `status` key no longer reads draft there either.
- **The Trigger pill.** The kind comes from `resolveFlowTriggerKind` (`@objectstack/spec/automation`, the authoring-time mirror of the engine's binding resolution, in the engine's precedence). A record kind shows the Start node's `triggerType` event and its `objectName`; a time-relative sweep shows its object; schedule and API show their kind; when no kind resolves (a manual or screen flow) the pill falls back to the flow `type`, as before. The words are the Start node inspector's own option labels (`fieldsForNodeType('start')` localized by `localizeFlowFields`), so the header and the inspector name one trigger one way, in en and zh.
- **Not running here.** Only an enabled row with a declared `triggerType` and `bound: false` reads it: the contract's "declared trigger type has no registered trigger" (or a deployment policy). A flow that declares no trigger runs when invoked and keeps `On`. The chip is grey; nothing is styled as an error.

## Measured: what `_status` serves on 17.7.0

The published `@objectstack/service-automation@17.7.0` engine (installed into a scratch directory), `getFlowRuntimeStates()` — the rows `GET /api/v1/automation/_status` passes through — with `OS_AUTOMATION_SCHEDULED_WORK_ENABLED` unset and the `record_change` and `schedule` triggers registered:

| Flow | Row |
|---|---|
| `record-after-update` on `task`, no `status` key | `enabled: true, bound: true, status: "draft", triggerType: "record_change", object: "task"` |
| the same with `status: "draft"` | identical: armed |
| schedule flow, no `status` key | `enabled: true, bound: false, status: "draft", triggerType: "schedule", reason: "disabled by deployment policy — package-authored scheduled work is off on this deployment …"` |
| Start declares nothing (manual) | `enabled: true, bound: false, status: "draft"` — no `triggerType`, no `reason` |
| record flow with `status: "obsolete"` | `enabled: false, bound: false, status: "obsolete", triggerType: "record_change", object: "task"` — no `reason` |
| Studio's new flow (`status: "obsolete"`, no trigger) | `enabled: false, bound: false, status: "obsolete"` |
| `type: "api"` with no api trigger registered | `enabled: true, bound: false, status: "draft", triggerType: "api", reason: "no 'api' trigger is registered — …"` |

Readings:
- The header's "draft" was the spec's own default: `FlowSchema.status` defaults to `draft`, the engine stores the parsed value, and arms `draft` exactly like `active`.
- The distinction PM hypothesis 3 asked for (no declared trigger versus deployment policy) is on the wire as `triggerType`: absent on a manual flow, present on every declared trigger. On 17.7.0 every enabled, unbound row with a `triggerType` also carries a `reason`; the title falls back to "Enabled, but its trigger is not armed on this deployment" only for an older backend that sends none.

## The one fork: the new flow's default — the default follows the bar

A flow created with *New* is saved with `status: 'obsolete'`; the bar's copy stays.
- **Real business need.** Measured: `doCreateFlow` is Studio's only flow producer (`save('flow'` has one non-test call site); it wrote no `status`; the spec defaults that to `draft`; the 17.7.0 engine arms `draft` (rows above). A package publish publishes every draft in the package, so a half-built record-triggered flow was armed on live records the first time anything in its package was published. The bar names that risk.
- **Long-term soundness.** The intent is now explicit metadata, in the value the Studio switch already writes for Off, and the one the engine's own boot hint names ("set status: 'active' to make intent explicit, or 'obsolete' to disable"). No new vocabulary, and no reader that interprets an absent key.
- **Preventing AI mistakes.** An automation an AI drafts in Studio cannot fire until a person flips it on. Changing the copy instead would have kept "armed on the next publish" as the silent default.
- **Startup focus.** One key on one producer, no new surface. The cost: `obsolete` is a lifecycle word for a flow that was never live; it is the spec's only off value (`draft` and `active` both arm).

## Problems: a note, not a problem

The not-running state shows in the Problems panel as a note above the list: the label and the reason, grey, dashed border. It is not a problem row: it is not counted in the Problems badge, not styled as an error or a warning, and the structural verdict ("No problems — this flow is structurally valid") stands beneath it. A deployment policy is an operator's fact, not an authoring defect. Off and manual flows get no note.

## Tests and gates (head `26ec168`)

New pins:
- `StudioDesignSurface.flowStatusTruth-11779.test.tsx`, through the real `AutomationsPillar` and the real registered `FlowPreview`, with a `_status` router double: the record flow's Trigger reads `Record updated · task`; schedule reads `Schedule (cron)`, manual falls back to `autolaunched`; the no-`status` published flow reads `On` in the rail and the header, never draft (the control); the unbound schedule flow reads `Not running here` in both, titled with the reason, and not `On`; Problems shows the note with the reason, uncounted, beside "No problems"; the manual flow reads `On` and gets no note (the control); a flow the engine has no row for reads `Unpublished draft`; *New* saves `status: obsolete`, `FlowSchema.safeParse` succeeds on the saved body, and the switch reads `Disabled` under the "Off by default" bar.
- `FlowPreview.headerPills-11779.test.tsx`: the pills with no runtime provider (record event and object, the zh inspector words, time-relative with its object, the type fallback; no `status` and `draft` read `Enabled`, `obsolete` reads `Disabled`).
- `flow-problems.runStatus-11779.test.ts`: the derivation table, including the disabled row, the runtime row outranking the draft, and that no reading is an error tone.

Updated pins: the objectui#11281 cases in `FlowStatusDot.test.tsx` and `StudioDesignSurface.railUnboundReason-11281.test.tsx` held a policy-unbound flow at a green `On`; they now read `Not running here` (the reason-verbatim and manual-flow controls are kept). The 11124, 11546, 11553 and 11204 pillar suites waited on the raw `active` Status pill; they now wait on its derived `Enabled`. The plain-language pin (objectui#11659) covers the three new rows.

Runs, all at `6916515` unless stated, from the worktree root:
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/ …` (plus `src/__tests__/`, the console `StudioRoute` suites and the i18n suites that read the touched modules): Test Files 217 passed (217), Tests 2287 passed.
- The rest of `metadata-admin` (`__tests__/`, `datasource/`, `external/`, `inspectors/`, the 165 root test files): Test Files 303 passed (303), Tests 3597 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the 15 touched files: 0 errors; per-file warning counts equal to the base commit (`d53fd02`).
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:spec-symbols`, `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: all exit 0 (verdict lines in the report).
- Declared narrowing: app-shell has more test files than the foreground cap runs; the files outside `studio-design/`, `metadata-admin/` and `src/__tests__/` were not run locally (a `git grep` for direct imports of the touched modules found none beyond those run). CI's `pnpm test` runs them.

## Ablation

The old Trigger pill source put back (`value={translateFlowMeta('type', String(d.type ?? 'autolaunched'), locale)}` over `value={flowTriggerLabel(d, nodes, locale)}`) through `ablation-replace.mjs`. First leg at `cd562f5` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `1404ef239c15` → `f12c7b8d4439`), running the two 11779 pill files: 5 failed, 10 passed — the record (en and zh), time-relative, record-through-the-pillar and schedule pins red; the type-fallback control and every status pin green. Restore proven: blob back to `1404ef239c15` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. Second leg at `26ec168` (blob `172f1cbf7090` → `7bfb27b575ab`): the same 5 red / 10 green; restore proven: blob back to `172f1cbf7090` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Acceptance notes

- **File surface.** Every edit is inside the claim's list. `FlowRuntimeContext` and the derivation sit in `flow-problems.ts` (listed, and the component-free module the preview and the panel already share); a dedicated module would be a cleaner home but is outside the claimed surface. Its objectui#11772 note said "React-free module"; with `createContext` imported it now says "component-free". The context first sat in `ProblemsPanel.tsx` and moved because `react-refresh/only-export-components` flagged it there.
- **`skeletons.ts` untouched.** `status: 'obsolete'` is added in `doCreateFlow`, not in `buildFlowSkeleton`, to stay inside the surface, so `createConformance.test.ts`'s skeleton gate does not see the key; the new pillar pin parses the body `doCreateFlow` actually saves with `FlowSchema`. Moving the key into the skeleton is a one-line follow-up for whoever next touches that file. carrier: none named.
- **Setup's Packaged automation page** (objectui#9217) reads the same `_status` rows through its own projection (`packagedFlows.ts`); it is not moved onto this derivation here. Noted, not filed.
- **Not measured:** the rendered pages in a browser (the DOM is pinned through the real pillar and preview; no screenshot run), and the app-shell test files outside the directories above (CI).
